key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially suppresses interfacial recombination but accelerates thermal degradation, with losses spreading into the perovskite absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive monitoring can help engineers assess whether interface passivation delivers durable benefits under thermal stress.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe depth-dependent photoluminescence responses.
Compare PEABF4-treated and untreated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret decay signatures using diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: Photoluminescence measurements indicate reduced fullerene-deposition-induced interfacial losses after treatment but faster degradation during thermal aging, with simulations supporting interface-versus-bulk interpretations.
watch_item: Depth attribution relies on diffusion–recombination modeling; the abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
